title: Irregular present: andare, venire, stare, uscire, dare
rule: Five high-frequency irregular verbs. The noi and voi forms are regular; the other four forms change the stem. Learn each as a chant.

items.t: Vado a Lecce. Vado in Puglia. Vado al mare. Vado da Dora.
items.n: I go to Lecce. To Puglia. To the sea. To Dora's.
items.note: a + city, in + region, al + place, da + person

items.n: Let's go! Shall we go home?

items.t: Come va? — Va bene. Tutto va bene.
items.n: How's it going? — Fine. Everything's fine.
I'm going to get the bread.
items.note: andare a + infinitive: going to do

items.t: Vieni con me? Vengo da Toronto. Viene dal Canada.
items.n: Are you coming with me? I come from Toronto. He comes from Canada.

items.t: Vengo subito! Veniamo a cena domenica.
items.n: I'm coming right away! We're coming to dinner on Sunday.
Will you come and have a coffee?

items.t: Come stai? — Sto bene. Sto male. Sto così così.
items.n: How are you? — I'm well. I'm unwell. So-so.

items.t: Oggi sto a casa. Stiamo in un piccolo appartamento.
items.n: Today I'm staying home. We live in a small flat.
items.note: staying; in the south, also living

items.t: Stai attento! Sta' zitto! Stai tranquillo.
items.n: Be careful! Be quiet! Don't worry.

items.t: Esco di casa alle otto. Esce dall'ufficio all'una.
items.n: I leave the house at eight. He leaves the office at one.
Shall we go out tonight? Are you going out with Chiara?

items.t: Mi dai le chiavi? Do le viti a Dora. Dà un consiglio a tutti.
items.n: Will you give me the keys? I give the screws to Dora. He gives advice to everyone.

items.t: Dare del tu / del Lei. Dammi del tu!
items.n: To use tu / Lei with someone. Call me tu!

blocks.title: Accents that distinguish
blocks.text: [[dà]] (gives) vs [[da]] (from) · [[sta]] (is, stays) has no accent · [[do]] (I give) vs the musical note do. In writing, the accent on dà is required.

items.why: Venire is irregular, not an -isc- verb.

items.wrong: Vado a Dora. Vengo con tu.
items.right: Vado da Dora. Vengo con te.

items.q: Stasera ___ (noi, uscire)? — No, ___ (io, stare) a casa: ___ (venire) Chiara.
items.n: Shall we go out tonight? — No, I'm staying home: Chiara is coming.
